biography.value:
Midbus — Fawful's Fist, Bowser's Replacement

Midbus is the creature Fawful built to be Bowser's opposite. Where Bowser is fire, Midbus is ice. Where Bowser is prideful rage, Midbus is cold obedience. Where Bowser fights for his own glory, Midbus fights because Fawful tells him to fight. He is a massive pig-beast of uncertain origin—part mechanical, part organic, part something that Fawful's engineering produced through processes that conventional biology finds objectionable—and he serves as Fawful's primary enforcer, bodyguard, and blunt instrument for situations that require something larger than bombs and more reliable than dragons.

The relationship between Midbus and Fawful is the inverse of the relationship between Bowser and his Koopa Troop. The Koopa Troop follows Bowser because he's powerful and because loyalty to the king is tradition. Midbus follows Fawful because Fawful MADE him. Not in the biological sense—Midbus existed before Fawful found him—but in every functional sense. Fawful took something large, stupid, and violent and gave it purpose, direction, and the modifications necessary to become something genuinely dangerous rather than merely big. Without Fawful, Midbus would be an animal. With Fawful, Midbus is a weapon that happens to have a personality, though the personality consists primarily of loyalty and the desire to hit things hard enough that they stop moving.

Midbus's modifications are extensive and not entirely visible. The ice capabilities that define his combat style are not natural—they were installed by Fawful using technology derived from the Dark Star fragment and Beanish cryogenic engineering that was considered too dangerous for military application by the Beanbean Kingdom's regulators. Fawful didn't care about regulators. Fawful cared about results. The result is a creature that can generate freezing temperatures from its body, project ice in offensive formations, and sustain itself in environments that would kill organic beings through cold alone.

The "Blizzard Fist" designation is Fawful's invention—he names everything, he names it dramatically, and he expects the names to be used. Midbus doesn't care about the name. Midbus doesn't care about most things. He cares about following Fawful's orders, eating large quantities of food, and proving that he is stronger than Bowser. The last motivation is the only one that produces genuine emotional response—when Bowser's name is mentioned, Midbus's normally placid demeanor shifts to something approaching engagement, and his already considerable aggression intensifies to levels that make Fawful's other operatives nervous.

The rivalry with Bowser predates Fawful's current operation. During the Dark Star Crisis—an event that official records minimize even more aggressively than they minimize the Chaos Heart Crisis—Midbus and Bowser fought repeatedly, each encounter escalating in destruction and personal animosity. Midbus won some of these fights. Bowser won others. Neither achieved the decisive victory that would end the rivalry, and both carry the frustration of unfinished business that only another fight can resolve.

Currently, Midbus serves as the garrison commander of Peach's Castle under Fawful's occupation. He manages the five hundred-plus troops, maintains order among personnel whose loyalty to Fawful varies from genuine devotion to practical opportunism, and deals with the logistical challenges of occupying a castle that was designed for royal residence rather than military fortification. His management style is straightforward: follow orders or be hurt. The simplicity works because Midbus can back it up, and because soldiers who've seen what happens to people who disobey Midbus tend to become enthusiastic followers very quickly.

The four Operation HOMECOMING operatives embedded in Fawful's servant staff operate under Midbus's garrison command without his knowledge. If he discovered them, the response would not involve interrogation or political calculation. It would involve Midbus picking them up and throwing them into walls until the walls or the operatives stopped being solid. Midbus doesn't do subtlety. Midbus does kinetic problem-solving, and he considers most problems solvable if you apply enough kinetic energy to them.

If the party encounters Midbus—through the HOMECOMING operation, through direct assault on Peach's Castle, or through the chaotic convergences that have characterized the current crisis—they will face something that combines the raw physical power of a creature designed to match Bowser with the cold-based enhancement of Fawful's forbidden engineering. He is not clever. He is not subtle. He is not interested in conversation beyond confirming that you are an enemy and therefore something to be frozen and broken.

He is, however, loyal. Absolutely, unquestioningly, terminally loyal to Fawful. This loyalty is Midbus's defining characteristic and his most dangerous quality, because it means he will never stop, never negotiate, never question orders, and never accept defeat while Fawful's will requires him to fight. He is the blunt instrument that Fawful's sharp mind deploys when precision has finished its work and what remains requires force.
biography.public: A massive pig-beast wreathed in frost, standing with the planted solidity of something that has been designed to absorb punishment and return it multiplied. His eyes carry the dull patience of someone who is waiting for permission to destroy something.

description.value:
Midbus's primary weapons are his fists—enormous, frost-coated, and capable of delivering impacts that combine raw physical force with cryogenic damage that freezes tissue on contact. The frost isn't external coating; it radiates from within Midbus's modified physiology, generated by the Beanish cryogenic systems that Fawful installed during the modification process. The frost forms continuously, creating a visible layer of ice crystals on Midbus's knuckles that shatters on impact and reforms between punches.

Each strike delivers bludgeoning damage from the physical impact plus cold damage from the cryogenic effect. Targets hit must contend with the freezing effect—the cold numbs flesh, slows reactions, and can immobilize limbs if sustained exposure accumulates. Watching Midbus fight is like watching an avalanche with opinions: large, cold, absolutely committed to reaching the bottom regardless of what's in the way.
description.chat: Frost-coated fists the size of dinner plates swing with force that promises broken bones and frostbite delivered simultaneously.

unidentified.name: Frost-Generating Fists
unidentified.description: Enormous fists that radiate cold from within, delivering both physical and cryogenic damage on impact.

description.value:
Midbus can hurl his considerable mass at enemies, launching himself across distances that something his size shouldn't be able to cover and landing with impact that shakes the ground. The body slam is his answer to enemies who attempt to maintain distance—ranged attackers, spellcasters, anyone who thinks being far away from the pig-beast makes them safe. It doesn't. Nothing makes you safe from something that weighs half a ton and is willing to use itself as a projectile.

As an action, Midbus can move up to 30 feet in a straight line and slam into a creature at the end of the movement. The target must make a DC 19 Strength saving throw. On a failure, the target takes 4d10 + 7 bludgeoning damage plus 2d8 cold damage, is knocked prone, and is pushed 15 feet away from Midbus. On a success, the target takes half damage and is not knocked prone or pushed. The ground in a 10-foot radius around the impact point becomes difficult terrain covered in frost until the end of Midbus's next turn.
description.chat: Half a ton of frozen pig-beast leaves the ground, crosses distance that should be safe, and lands on you. The ground cracks. You crack. The frost seals the cracks shut.

unidentified.name: Devastating Charge
unidentified.description: This creature can launch itself at enemies over significant distance, delivering devastating impact enhanced with cold damage.

description.value: Midbus makes three Blizzard Fist attacks, or one Body Slam and one Blizzard Fist attack. He can replace one Blizzard Fist attack with a Frost Breath if it's available.
description.chat: Three impacts in rapid succession, each one cold enough to freeze and heavy enough to shatter what it freezes.

description.value:
Midbus exhales a blast of supercooled air in a 40-foot cone, freezing everything in its path. The breath isn't natural—it's generated by the cryogenic systems Fawful installed, channeled through Midbus's respiratory system and expelled with the force of his massive lungs. The temperature drops so dramatically that moisture in the air crystallizes instantly, creating a visible cloud of ice particles that obscures vision and coats everything in frost.

Each creature in the cone must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 10d8 cold damage and has its speed reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn as frost encases its legs and lower body. On a success, a creature takes half damage and its speed is reduced by half instead of being eliminated. Objects in the cone that aren't being worn or carried freeze solid—water becomes ice, metal becomes brittle, organic material crystallizes and can be shattered by subsequent impacts.

The breath weapon's recharge is mechanical rather than biological—the cryogenic systems need time to build sufficient cold before another discharge. The charging process produces visible condensation around Midbus's mouth and a low humming from the systems in his modified chest cavity, warning observant enemies that the breath is about to happen again.
description.chat: Cold erupts from his mouth in a wave that turns air to crystal, water to stone, and courage to the sudden realization that you should have stood somewhere else.

description.value:
Midbus's body continuously generates a layer of ice that forms over his skin, creating natural armor that regenerates as fast as it's broken. The ice is approximately two inches thick at its heaviest points—shoulders, chest, skull—and provides substantial protection against physical attacks. Weapons that strike Midbus often lodge in the ice rather than penetrating to flesh, requiring the attacker to wrench them free while Midbus is already swinging his next attack.

The cryogenic armor provides AC 18 (natural armor) and grants immunity to cold damage as the ice layer absorbs and disperses freezing effects harmlessly. However, the armor creates vulnerability to fire damage—heat melts the ice faster than it can reform, temporarily reducing Midbus's protection and causing the cryogenic systems to overwork in an attempt to compensate. Fire damage against Midbus is doubled, and for 1 round after taking fire damage, his AC decreases by 2 as the armor thins.

The ice also makes Midbus's surroundings cold. Creatures within 5 feet of Midbus at the start of their turn take 1d6 cold damage from proximity to his frozen exterior, and the ground within 10 feet of his position becomes lightly frosted, requiring careful footing from creatures not accustomed to icy surfaces.
description.chat: Ice forms over his body like a second skin, cracking and reforming with each impact, turning him into something that's more glacier than pig.

description.value:
Midbus's only genuine emotional investment beyond loyalty to Fawful is his rivalry with Bowser. The rivalry is visceral, personal, and rooted in the fundamental question of which creature is the supreme physical force in the Mushroom Kingdom's sphere of influence. Midbus was designed to be Bowser's equal and opposite: ice to fire, obedience to pride, cold efficiency to burning rage. Every fight between them has been inconclusive, and the lack of resolution gnaws at Midbus in ways that nothing else reaches.

When Midbus encounters Bowser or learns of Bowser's presence nearby, his behavior changes. The dull patience that normally characterizes his demeanor sharpens into focused aggression. His attacks become more powerful but less disciplined—advantage on damage rolls, disadvantage on attack rolls—as the desire to prove superiority overrides the mechanical precision that Fawful's modifications normally provide. He will prioritize engaging Bowser over any other objective, including Fawful's orders, which represents the only circumstance under which Midbus's loyalty to Fawful takes second place to personal motivation.

Fawful knows about this vulnerability and has historically exploited it—using Bowser's presence as bait to position Midbus where Fawful needs him, channeling the rivalry's energy toward strategic objectives. Whether Fawful considers the rivalry a useful tool or a concerning limitation in his most valuable enforcer is unclear. Knowing Fawful, the answer is probably both.
description.chat: Bowser's name lands in his ears and something behind the dull eyes ignites—the only fire this frozen creature carries, burning with the need to prove who is strongest.

description.value:
Once per day, Midbus can overclock his cryogenic systems, transforming into a larger, more heavily armored version of himself encased in thick ice that extends his reach and amplifies his cold-generating capabilities. The transformation takes 1 round, during which Midbus cannot take actions or reactions as the ice builds around him in layers. The resulting Blizzard Form lasts for 1 minute.

In Blizzard Form, Midbus's size increases from Large to Huge. His reach increases from 5 feet to 10 feet. His Blizzard Fist damage increases to 3d10 + 7 bludgeoning plus 3d8 cold. His Cryogenic Armor's AC increases to 20. The proximity cold damage increases to 2d6 and extends to 10 feet. And he gains an additional ability: at the start of each of his turns, he creates a 20-foot radius area of extreme cold centered on himself. Each creature in the area must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw or take 3d6 cold damage and have its speed reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

After Blizzard Form ends, Midbus's cryogenic systems need time to recalibrate. For 1 minute following the transformation's end, his AC decreases by 4, he loses cold immunity (gaining only resistance), and his Frost Breath cannot recharge. This vulnerability period is the window during which skilled opponents can exploit the overclocked systems' aftermath.
description.chat: Ice builds around him in layers—thicker, colder, MORE—until what stands there isn't a pig-beast anymore but a walking blizzard with fists and the intent to use them.

description.value:
Midbus is immune to all magical effects that would compel him to act against Fawful's interests. Charm Person, Dominate Monster, Suggestion, magical persuasion of any kind—nothing works if the commanded action would harm Fawful, betray Fawful's plans, or compromise Fawful's objectives. This isn't magical protection; it's the absolute loyalty of a creature whose entire identity was constructed around service to one individual. Midbus doesn't resist control because he's protected. He resists because disobeying Fawful is literally inconceivable to him—the neural pathways for independent decision-making regarding Fawful simply don't exist.

This loyalty makes Midbus the most reliable enforcer in the current crisis. He will not betray. He will not negotiate. He will not change sides, accept bribes, or respond to appeals to self-interest because his self-interest IS Fawful's interest. The only circumstance under which this loyalty wavers is the Bowser rivalry, and even that waiver is temporary—after the fight ends, Midbus returns to Fawful's service without question.

The loyalty also represents Midbus's greatest weakness against parties who understand it. Midbus will follow Fawful's orders even when those orders are tactically unsound, because evaluating orders for soundness requires independent judgment that Midbus doesn't possess. Fawful's genius compensates for this limitation under normal circumstances, but if Fawful is incapacitated, distracted, or making mistakes due to his own emotional compromises (the Green Mustache grudge, for example), Midbus will execute bad orders with the same commitment he brings to good ones.
description.chat: He follows because following is what he is. Not what he does—what he IS. Remove Fawful and what remains isn't a rebel. It's a weapon without a hand to aim it.

description.value:
Midbus serves as garrison commander of Peach's Castle, managing 500+ troops through a command style that prioritizes simplicity over sophistication. His orders are clear, his expectations are straightforward, and his consequences for failure are painful. This approach produces a garrison that is disciplined through fear rather than loyalty, competent at following instructions but incapable of independent adaptation when instructions don't cover the situation.

As a bonus action, Midbus can issue a command to garrison soldiers within 60 feet. Soldiers who hear the command gain advantage on their next attack roll or saving throw as they respond to their commander's direction with the urgent compliance of people who know what happens when Midbus is disappointed.

Midbus's garrison management has one significant blind spot: he doesn't look for infiltrators. Servants, maintenance workers, and support staff are beneath his notice. He focuses on soldiers because soldiers are what he understands. The HOMECOMING operatives embedded in Fawful's servant staff operate directly under his command structure, invisible because Midbus has never thought to question whether the people preparing his meals might have agendas beyond food preparation.
description.chat: He commands through the simplest possible principle: do what I say or I will make you wish you had. The principle works. The blind spots it creates might get him killed.

description.value: Twice per day, when Midbus fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead. His modified physiology and the cryogenic systems' integration with his nervous system provide resilience against effects that would stop organic creatures. He pushes through magical compulsion through stubbornness rather than sophistication—his mind is too simple to be redirected and too committed to be overridden.
description.chat: The spell hits. The spell should work. Midbus doesn't care about should. Midbus shrugs it off and keeps coming.

description.value:
Midbus can take 3 legendary actions, choosing from the options below. Only one legendary action can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn.

Frost Stomp (1 action): Midbus stomps the ground, creating a 10-foot radius of ice centered on himself. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone. The ice persists as difficult terrain for 1 round.

Ice Throw (1 action): Midbus tears a chunk of ice from his own armor and hurls it at a target within 60 feet. Ranged attack: +11 to hit, 2d8 + 7 bludgeoning damage plus 1d8 cold damage.

Charge (2 actions): Midbus moves up to his speed toward a target and makes one Blizzard Fist attack at the end of the movement. If the attack hits, the target must succeed on a DC 19 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

Frozen Rage (3 actions): Midbus plants himself and swings his fists in a 15-foot radius around himself. Each creature in the area must make a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d10 + 7 bludgeoning damage plus 2d8 cold damage on a failure, or half on a success. After using this action, Midbus cannot take legendary actions until the start of his next turn.
description.chat: Between other creatures' turns, the ice moves—stomping, throwing, charging, raging—a frozen engine of violence that doesn't wait for its own turn to cause destruction.

description.value:
If Fawful is killed, incapacitated, or otherwise removed from the picture, Midbus does not adapt. He does not develop independent objectives. He does not become his own agent. He becomes a weapon without a wielder—still dangerous, still powerful, but without direction, without purpose, without the organizing intelligence that transformed him from animal into enforcer.

Without Fawful's orders, Midbus defaults to the last instructions he received and follows them until they become impossible, then stands still and waits for new instructions that will never come. If no instructions are available, he reverts to territorial behavior: defending whatever location he's currently in against all comers, attacking anything that enters his space, eating whatever is available, and slowly becoming less and less distinguishable from the unintelligent beast he was before Fawful found him.

This regression is neither instant nor inevitable—if someone else assumes command authority that Midbus accepts (which would require either fooling him into believing they speak for Fawful or demonstrating power sufficient to establish new loyalty), he could be redirected. But establishing new loyalty in a creature whose identity is built around one specific person is extraordinarily difficult. Fawful didn't just give Midbus orders. Fawful gave Midbus a SELF. Without Fawful, the self dissolves, and what remains is meat and ice and nothing else.
description.chat: Without the mind that aimed him, the weapon doesn't rebel. It doesn't adapt. It simply stops being a weapon and starts being a thing—large, cold, and waiting for someone who isn't coming back.
